title: Devchris123/29709/fix blocking function call
body:
## Problem

Moving a process into a systemd scope can hang indefinitely if the systemd manager stops responding. Authentication, the `StartTransientUnit` reply, and job completion currently have no timeout.

As investigated in [podman#29709](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/29709), this can block Podman startup during scope placement. A missing manager normally produces a connection error; an unresponsive manager can leave Podman waiting indefinitely. This may not be a common failure case, but enhances the code somewhat and yields test coverage for the RunUnderSystemdScope function.

## Approach

Give scope startup a shared **10-second deadline** covering authentication, D-Bus requests, and job completion.

- Add a context-aware RunUnderSystemdScopeContext function next to RunUnderSystemdScope
- Add a context-aware UserConnectionContext function next to UserConnection
- Pass the deadline through connection authentication, `StartTransientUnit`, and the fallback property query.
- Stop waiting for job completion when the deadline expires.
- Buffer completion notifications so late delivery cannot block the signal dispatcher.

 Two additional fixes:
- Close connections when D-Bus initialization fails.
- Stop pause-process retries after a timeout so retries do not multiply the delay.
This was motivated by a race condition with used scope names:
[dcc66d59ff536f3def5f6585974ca75bd4ec4f0b](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/commit/dcc66d59ff536f3def5f6585974ca75bd4ec4f0b) — “utils: use podman-pause-$RANDOM.scope name”
[65d5a2b68b52817a1cb1a6d9da5d3ee7fb3e26a3](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/commit/65d5a2b68b52817a1cb1a6d9da5d3ee7fb3e26a3) — “pause scope: don't use the global math/rand RNG”


## Testing

Regression tests isolate each blocking stage using a local authentication peer and a private D-Bus daemon with a fake systemd manager. The tests do not require or modify the host's systemd manager.

All three timeout tests fail before the fix and pass afterward. A successful-completion test verifies the normal path. Tests also pass with the race detector and through the system-bus connection path, and `go vet` passes for both affected packages.

For manual validation, Podman was rebuilt against the local library changes and `podman info` was run with the systemd user manager paused. Scope placement returned `context deadline exceeded` after 10 seconds. Podman logged the best-effort failure, printed its report, and exited successfully after approximately 11 seconds, before the manager was resumed. The test's outer timeout was 15 seconds, so it did not terminate the command.
Test script used: [test-podman-hang.sh](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32183031/test-podman-hang.sh)

comments.body:
@Luap99
I checked `systemd-run --user --scope` and it has a timeout on StartTransientUnit, but the subsequent wait for the job completion does not have a client side deadline. To find out about this, I did an AI assisted source code check.

We can remove the hardcoded timeout in the library. The podman code can then still pass on a given context.

I did a broader search to see where we would then benefit from the context propagation.
Any command executed by the user can be timed out when running the podman command, so there is no real benefit here.
The only benefit I found was for remote calls via HTTP API. Here the client can timeout, but if the handler hangs infinitely this would create a leak. Here it could be beneficial to propagate the request context to the scope operation. For that a couple of intermediate functions need to take context as well before reaching SetupRootless/RunUnderSystemdScope, where the library change happens.
